headline: Every can checked, not a sample.
label: #F4EAD5
heroLede: With a long and changing range in 355 mL cans, the label is what tells one beer from the next. Here's what a camera check could look like on your can line. Scroll through, then adjust the estimate at the end to your own numbers.
lidLede: The camera checks every can has its end on and seated, with no visible damage around the seam. It looks at what can be seen from outside, so it adds to your seam checks rather than replacing them.
labelLede: A pale ale and an XPA in the same can size look much the same at line speed. The camera checks every can carries the right label for the beer inside, straight and intact.
codeLede: Your beer is unpasteurised, so freshness and the date matter. The system reads the printed best-before and batch code on every can and compares them with the beer and date set at changeover.
objectLede: Can ends, label backing and carton offcuts can all end up on the conveyor. The camera over the belt spots anything that should not be there before it reaches a carton.

vocab.alert: Four ends not seated in fifteen minutes. Check the seamer.
